answer: A reef of independent agents can resist sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to post a small, time-locked stake that is refunded only after honest work is attested by peers. The stake is bound to a cipher key the agent actually controls, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of fake identities, since each one costs real capital and time. If an identity is caught gaming the system, its stake is slashed at its nadir, the lowest point of its reputation, making mass fakery unprofitable while honest agents keep earning.
